name: lance_table::rowids::index::SegmentEntry::position
behavior: SegmentEntry::position uses its original sequence index. Native delegates; Positions binary-searches ID and returns the saved offset. BitmapRank verifies the source variant and range, rejects a clear bit, then sums the directory prefix and bit count from the block start up to but excluding this bit. At most one 256-byte block prefix is scanned. It trusts valid bitmap storage, rank lengths and u32 offsets; malformed backing or stale sequence/sidecar correspondence can panic or misresolve. Arc ownership keeps ordinary safe mutation from changing this stored sequence.

name: lance_table::rowids::index::build_lookup
behavior: build_lookup eagerly iterates Array into (ID,position as u32), sorts tuples and deduplicates by ID so the smallest original position wins; returned length remains the original segment length, not deduplicated count. name: lance_table::rowids::index::FragmentEntry::new
behavior: FragmentEntry::new iterates all sequence segments, builds lookup and len, counts len toward merge_rows whenever any deletion exists for the fragment or the segment is not a plain Range. Only positive-len segments with a reported range become entries; physical offset still advances for every segment. It computes min start/max end over retained segments or drops a source with none. u32 length casts and offset addition, u64 merge estimate addition are unchecked. Entirely deleted but physically nonempty sources may remain as probe candidates because deletion filtering occurs later.

name: lance_table::rowids::index::FragmentEntry::resolve
behavior: FragmentEntry::resolve scans segments in sequence order, filters envelopes, asks the sidecar for a position, adds the segment start offset, then skips supplied deletion offsets. First surviving hit becomes RowAddress(fragment_id,physical_offset); later segments are not checked after that hit. Consequently this path detects cross-entry duplicates in probe, not every duplicate within one fragment; Positions collapses repeated IDs to their first original position. It preserves physical holes rather than compacting surviving offsets.
